category_title: Students exhibiting conflict avoidance in collaborative group work
scenario_title: Navigating group dynamics and uneven participation through public and private reflections
minimal_context: During a class session in an honors seminar, the tutor asks Joey to publicly share a metaphor describing his research team's progress with his peers.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Joey, please go ahead and publicly share the metaphor you wrote to describe your research team and your progress.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I described my team as an engine. This engine runs really well on three cylinders, but when the other two spark plug wires are attached, the engine acts almost as if it is supercharged.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: What does that mean for your group's dynamics?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Up to this point the engine is running really well but there is so much more performance possible when all the spark plug wires contribute spark.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: This is an opportunity to encourage your teammates to become more engaged with the project. Do you have anything else to add about the deadlines or participation?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Looks uncomfortable) No, we are having relative success. I just want to encourage everyone to fully engage in the research process. Everything is fine.
